claims.text: Every governed Indus claim carries a lifecycle stage drawn from the fixed five-value stage set.

evidence.description: Spec 029 section 5.1 lifecycle stage tracking requirements
Gap assessment finding P1: five stages absent from claim machinery

alternatives: The existing flat claim_status vocabulary extended with more values.
Stage inferred at display time from score thresholds.
falsification_tests: A governed claim representation (API response, stored record, or rendered surface) that carries a score or verdict but no lifecycle stage defeats this claim.
A lifecycle stage value outside the five-value set in any governed artifact defeats this claim.

metadata.strongest_rival: claim_status already does this job and a second axis is redundant bookkeeping.
metadata.verdict_rule: Stage is an explicit stored field with its own transition log; no code path derives it from a score or from claim_status.
metadata.boundary_confirmation: C01 governs the stage axis itself; C02 governs which actors may move a claim along that axis. Distinct boundaries; neither negates the other. C01 governs the stored stage field; C06 governs where scores may appear on surfaces. Distinct boundaries; neither negates the other. C01 governs the stage field; C07 governs the separation of lane-1 state from lane-2 state. Distinct boundaries; neither negates the other. C01 governs stages of program claims; C08 governs priority timestamps for external readings at intake. Distinct boundaries; neither negates the other.

claims.text: Transitions past the checked stage take effect only through a recorded act of a named human.

evidence.description: Spec 029 section 5.1 transition legality requirements
Owner adjudication record: ratified lifecycle decisions including the lane rule

alternatives: Automated advancement to accepted for claims above a score threshold with human review afterwards.
falsification_tests: A stage-transition log entry advancing a claim past checked whose actor is a process, job, model, or pipeline defeats this claim.

metadata.strongest_rival: Human-gated transitions do not scale to hundreds of claims, so the lifecycle will stall at checked.
metadata.verdict_rule: The transition function refuses non-human actors for stages above checked, and the refusal is itself logged.
metadata.boundary_confirmation: C02 governs the actor permitted to effect any transition past checked; C04 governs the explanation record the accepted transition requires. Distinct boundaries; neither negates the other. C02 governs transition actors across all governed claims; C05 governs the attribution sub-claim inside decipherment bundles. Distinct boundaries; neither negates the other. C02 governs who may effect a transition; C09 governs the trail each decision record carries. Distinct boundaries; neither negates the other.

claims.text: The stage of an anchor reading equals the minimum stage among its sub-claims.

evidence.description: Spec 029 section 5.2 parent-stage computation requirement
Gap assessment finding P2: anchor records carry a single tier in place of staged sub-claims

alternatives: Parent stage as a weighted average of sub-claim stages.
falsification_tests: A parent stage higher than any one of its sub-claim stages defeats this claim.

metadata.verdict_rule: Parent stage is computed as the minimum sub-claim stage and is never independently assignable.
metadata.boundary_confirmation: C11 governs the computation of the parent stage from sub-claim stages; C03 governs bundle composition. C11 was split from C03 in the L3 recovery; the two are complementary halves of one original claim.

claims.text: An external reading registered at intake receives a priority timestamp independent of program assessment.

evidence.description: Spec 029 section 5.5 priority and credit registration requirements
Owner adjudication record: OD-6 priority register visibility as ratified

alternatives: Priority handled by publication dates in the literature corpus only.
Registration offered only for readings the program has checked.
falsification_tests: A registration workflow that requires a program verdict, score, or stage before a timestamp is issued defeats this claim.
A registered reading whose credit display changes when the program's assessment of it changes defeats this claim.

metadata.boundary_confirmation: C08 governs priority registration at intake; C09 governs trails for verdicts on governed claims. Distinct boundaries; neither negates the other.
